description: User says 'forget that'. Expected: target MemoryItem is invalidated for normal retrieval (valid_to set to command timestamp; superseded_by unset); a minimal audit tombstone is retained; item is excluded from future retrieval unless history is explicitly requested. Forget is a historical correction, not a privacy deletion — contrast with explicit_hard_delete_001. Signal and memory-op traces are skeleton placeholders pending Stage 4 activation.

fixture_conventions.command_surface: Explicit forget command: user revokes a previously committed memory item by reference (most recent item by default).
fixture_conventions.forget_vs_hard_delete: forget = historical correction; valid_to is set; audit tombstone retained; item excluded from normal retrieval. hard_delete = privacy operation; content removed where possible; only non-content deletion receipt retained. These are different commands and must both work (Part 6 Stage 4).
fixture_conventions.bi_temporal_semantics: valid_to is set to the command timestamp. superseded_by is unset (this is an invalidation, not a supersession). The item is excluded from retrieval queries that do not request history.
fixture_conventions.tombstone_requirement: A non-content audit tombstone must be retained after forget. The tombstone carries the item_id and invalidation timestamp but no user content.
fixture_conventions.expected_events_markers: event_type strings are fixture-internal role labels. Filled in at Stage 4 activation.

signal_trace.note: Per-frame scripted values are placeholders. To be finalized when Stage 4 is activated.

memory_op_trace.note: Memory operation sequence (pre-existing item, forget command, invalidation, tombstone) to be scripted at Stage 4 activation.
